v2Preview.title: The new engine is playable
v2Preview.description: Four cases written for the V2 engine: constraint propagation, five-level hints, an investigator’s notebook, and a murderer derived from the plan instead of written in advance.

case.selectHint: Click a suspect, then click a cell to place them (dragging works too).
case.rowColumnHint: 💡 "Row" and "column" are counted across the whole floor plan (like coordinates), not just the suspect's room. "North/south/east/west of X" works the same way: relative to the whole plan.
case.giveUpButton: Give up and see the solution

hint.none: Nothing left to reveal: your plan already reflects every available deduction.

l1.rowColEliminationRow: Someone is already placed on row {{index}}: that row is closed to everyone else.
l1.rowColEliminationCol: Someone is already placed on column {{index}}: that column is closed to everyone else.
l1.lockedCandidatesRow: Someone still unlocated has no possible cells left outside row {{index}}. That row is reserved for them.
l1.lockedCandidatesCol: Someone still unlocated has no possible cells left outside column {{index}}. That column is reserved for them.
l1.relationalFilter: A clue linking two people already rules cells out, even though neither of them is placed yet.
l1.relationalExclusion: Someone denies a link to another person: wherever that link would be unavoidable, they cannot have been.
l1.zoneExclusivityTaken: Someone swears they were alone in their room, yet another person is bound to be in it: that is not where they were.
l1.zoneExclusivityClaimedAlone: A room is already claimed by someone who says they were alone in it: it closes to everyone else.
l1.zoneCompany: Someone swears they were not alone: a room nobody could still join them in is therefore ruled out for them.
l1.nakedSingle: Look for the person who has only one possible cell left.

l2.rowColElimination: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink, through the one-person-per-row-and-column rule.
l2.lockedCandidates: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink: someone else, without even being located, denies them a row or a column.
l2.relationalFilter: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink, because of the clue tying them to another person.
l2.relationalExclusion: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink: on those cells the link they deny would hold, wherever the other person ends up.
l2.zoneExclusivity: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink: a whole room is closed to them, because it cannot hold two.
l2.zoneCompany: It is {{person}}'s options that shrink: in that room, nobody could have been with them.
l2.nakedSingle: {{person}} has only one possible cell left. Up to you to find which one.

l3.rowTaken: {{person}} cannot stay on row {{row}}: {{by}} is already there.
l3.colTaken: {{person}} cannot stay on column {{col}}: {{by}} is already there.
l3.confinedToRow: Every cell still possible for {{confinedPerson}} sits on row {{row}}, so that row is reserved for them and {{person}} must leave it.
l3.confinedToCol: Every cell still possible for {{confinedPerson}} sits on column {{col}}, so that column is reserved for them and {{person}} must leave it.
l3.relationalWithPerson: {{person}} was with {{other}}: only the cells in a room where {{other}} can still be remain.
l3.relationalDirection: How {{person}} lies relative to {{other}} rules out the cells incompatible with every position {{other}} can still take.
l3.relationalDistance: The exact gap between {{person}} and {{other}} rules out the cells incompatible with every position {{other}} can still take.
l3.relational: The clue tying {{person}} to {{other}} rules out the incompatible cells.
l3.relationalNotWithPerson: {{person}} was not with {{other}}: on those cells they would share {{other}}'s room, wherever {{other}} turns out to be.
l3.relationalNotDirection: {{person}} denies lying that way relative to {{other}}: on those cells it would be true for every position {{other}} can still take.
l3.relationalNotDistance: {{person}} denies that exact gap to {{other}}: on those cells it would hold for every position {{other}} can still take.
l3.relationalNot: {{person}} denies the link they are credited with to {{other}}: on those cells that link would be unavoidable.
l3.zoneTaken: {{person}} claims to have been alone, yet {{by}} is bound to be in {{zone}}: so {{person}} was not there.
l3.zoneClaimedAlone: {{by}} was alone in {{zone}}: nobody else can be there, {{person}} included.
l3.zoneNeedsCompany: {{person}} was not alone, yet nobody else can be in {{zone}} with them: so that is not where they were.
l3.onlyOptionLeft: Every other cell for {{person}} has already been eliminated.

l4.rowColEliminationRow: {{by}} already occupies row {{row}}, so {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.rowColEliminationCol: {{by}} already occupies column {{col}}, so {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.lockedCandidatesRow: {{confinedPerson}} can only be on row {{row}}, which is therefore reserved for them: {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.lockedCandidatesCol: {{confinedPerson}} can only be on column {{col}}, which is therefore reserved for them: {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.relationalFilter: The clue tying {{person}} to {{other}} is incompatible with {{cells}}: those cells fall.
l4.relationalExclusion: At {{cells}}, {{person}} could not have denied the link to {{other}}: wherever {{other}} can still be, it would hold. Those cells fall.
l4.zoneExclusivityTaken: {{by}} is bound to be in {{zone}}, where {{person}} claims to have been alone: {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.zoneExclusivityClaimedAlone: {{by}} was alone in {{zone}}: {{person}} cannot be at {{cells}}.
l4.zoneCompany: Nobody can keep {{person}} company in {{zone}}: {{cells}} fall.
l4.nakedSingle: With every other cell eliminated, {{person}} must be at {{cell}}.

l5.nothingToPlace: No cell can be settled for certain yet: keep eliminating.

1.label: Beginner
1.description: Every suspect can be worked out alone, one direct clue is enough.

2.label: Easy
2.description: A few suspects need two clues combined.

3.label: Medium
3.description: You need to place some suspects before you can deduce others.

4.label: Advanced
4.description: Several deduction chains, plus at least two suspects who only resolve relative to each other.

5.label: Hard
5.description: Few direct clues: you'll need to reason by elimination across nearly the whole grid.

6.label: Fiendish
6.description: The biggest cast, the longest chains, and even the fact that no room is empty becomes something you must use.

goal.title: The goal: unmask the murderer
goal.body: You are handed the plan of a place divided into rooms, the people who were there that night — suspects and one victim — and what each of them said. Nobody lies. Your job is to place everyone on the plan.
goal.note: The culprit's name is written nowhere: the correct plan is what points at them. The murderer is whoever ended up alone with the victim in a room.
goal.figAlone: The lounge holds only the victim and Alba: Alba is the murderer.
goal.figCrowd: Three people in the lounge: nobody was alone with the victim.

rowcol.title: One person per row and per column
rowcol.body: This is the tightest rule in the game. Two people never share a row, and never share a column. Placing someone therefore denies a whole row and a whole column to everybody else.
rowcol.note: Walls change nothing: the rule holds across the entire plan, even between two rooms with no way through. It holds for the victim too.
rowcol.figClash: Alba and Bruno are on the same row: impossible, even in two different rooms.
rowcol.figClear: Everyone with their own row and column: this plan stands.

neighbour.title: "Next to" is not "with"
neighbour.body: "Next to" means immediately left, right, above or below — never diagonally — and in the same room. "With" simply means in the same room, at any distance at all.
neighbour.note: So two cells touching across a wall are not "next to" each other. "Further north than X", on the other hand, is counted across the whole plan: it does not mean "in the same column".
neighbour.figNext: Alba is directly above the plant, in the same room: she is next to it.
neighbour.figWall: The two cells touch, but a wall separates them: that is not "next to".
neighbour.figWith: Alba is "with" Bruno: same room, however far apart.

objects.title: Furniture and windows
objects.body: Some objects can be stood on — a bunk, a bench, a rug. Others are impassable: their cells are hatched and nobody ever stands there. An object can cover several cells and still be one single thing.
objects.note: A clue therefore does not always name a single cell, and that is deliberate: the other clues are what settle it.
objects.figBed: "On the bunk": three possible cells, not one.
objects.figWindow: A window is an opening in the wall. "In front of the window": every cell facing it.
objects.figBlocked: Nobody climbs onto the table — but a clue can perfectly well talk about it.

tools.title: Your tools
tools.body: The plan works like paper: place a person once you are sure, pencil out the cells you have ruled them out of. Nothing is final until you solve.
tools.note: Clicking a person already on the plan picks them back up. Dragging works too.
tools.figMarks: Alba is placed; Bruno has been pencilled out of two cells.

place.label: Place
place.help: Pick a person, then their cell on the plan.

cross.label: Cross out
cross.help: Pencil mode: mark the cells where a person cannot have been. A pencil mark is only a note — it blocks nothing.

hint.label: 💡 Hint
hint.help: Five levels, from a nudge ("look for the person with only one cell left") all the way to revealing a position.

notebook.label: Take stock
notebook.help: For each suspect, says what you can already prove from what you've placed and crossed out yourself — never further than your own reasoning.

verdict.title: Solving
verdict.body: Once everybody is on the plan, the "Solve" button lights up. The engine then compares your plan to the one and only possible plan.
verdict.note: A wrong grid costs you nothing: you pick up exactly where you left off.
verdict.figWrong: Wrong grid: every person is marked right or wrong, and you carry on.
verdict.figRight: Correct grid: the victim's room holds just one other person — the culprit reveals themselves.

picker.heading: Cases for the new engine
picker.subheading: The V2 engine reasons like a player: it never guesses. Every case below is solvable by deduction alone, and the murderer is written nowhere — a correct plan is what names them.

play.placeHint: Pick a person, then a cell on the plan (dragging works too).
play.crossHint: Pencil mode: pick a person, then click the cells where they cannot have been.
play.solveBlocked: {{placed}} / {{total}} people placed: the plan has to be complete.
play.testimoniesNote: Nobody lies: everything stated here is true.
play.victimLine: The victim. They were alone with their killer.
play.blockedNote: Hatched cells hold an impassable object: nobody stands there.
play.rulesNote: 💡 One person per row and per column, across the whole plan. "Row", "column" and "further north/south/east/west than X" are counted across the whole plan, not just within a room — and "further north" does not mean "in the same column".

trail.heading: The thread of the case
trail.waiting: Nothing established yet. Place someone or cross out a cell, and the first deduction will be written here.
trail.revealsLeft_one: One more person to locate before the murderer names themselves.
trail.revealsLeft_other: {{count}} more people to locate before the murderer names themselves.
trail.lastThread: Everyone is located: all that is left is to follow the reasoning to its end.
trail.closed: The chain has been followed all the way to its end. All that is left is the verdict.

placement.open: Nothing forces them there yet — for now it's a guess.
placement.refuted: What you've already established rules out this cell.

exclusion.refuted_one: One of your crossed-out cells is refuted:
exclusion.refuted_other: {{count}} of your crossed-out cells are refuted:

candidates.forced: Only one cell is still possible: it can be deduced right now.

result.murdererWhy: {{name}} is the only person who was in {{zone}} with {{victim}}.
result.noMurderer: Nobody is convicted: the victim did not spend the night alone with a single suspect.
result.whyRowClash: this cell shares a row with {{name}}, who already has it.
result.whyColClash: this cell shares a column with {{name}}, who already has it.
result.whyFallback: every clue holds here on its own — it’s the combination with the rest of the plan that doesn’t work.

beginner.label: Beginner
beginner.description: Every deduction follows directly from the previous one.

intermediate.label: Intermediate
intermediate.description: Several deductions have to be chained before a cell falls.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.description: Long chains, and one step almost everything else depends on.

expert.label: Expert
expert.description: The finest techniques, across nearly the whole grid.
